strings.name: Fumio Kishida
strings.role: Politician · former Japanese prime minister and foreign minister
strings.summary: Kishida entered the Diet after banking and work as a parliamentary secretary, building a career representing Hiroshima. As foreign minister he worked on US-Japan relations and Obama’s Hiroshima visit. Prime minister from 2021 to 2024, he advanced defense, economic-security and energy-policy changes and hosted the Hiroshima G7 summit. Amid party funding scandals and declining support, he left the leadership contest and premiership, remaining a representative.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A former Japanese prime minister and foreign minister who advanced defense and economic-security changes and participated in nuclear disarmament and multilateral diplomacy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Tokyo, Japan; his political career is closely associated with Hiroshima.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated in law from Waseda University in 1982; worked at the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, then as a parliamentary secretary.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Defense and economic security
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advanced the 2022 National Security Strategy, defense-policy changes and economic-security institutions as prime minister.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Hiroshima and multilateral diplomacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Worked on nuclear disarmament and hosted the 2023 G7 summit in Hiroshima.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Left the premiership
strings.timeline.t1.text: After declining to contest the LDP leadership, handed over to Shigeru Ishiba and remained a representative.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Hosted Hiroshima G7 summit
strings.timeline.t2.text: G7 leaders met in Hiroshima to discuss Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and economic security.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Cabinet approved security strategies
strings.timeline.t3.text: The cabinet adopted new strategic documents calling for stronger counterstrike capabilities and defense spending.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became prime minister
strings.timeline.t4.text: Took office after winning the LDP leadership, then formed another cabinet following the general election.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Began extended foreign-minister tenure
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became foreign minister in Abe’s second administration, serving until 2017.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First entered the cabinet
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became minister of state for special missions, including Okinawa and Northern Territories affairs.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First elected to the House
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won his first House of Representatives election, beginning a long Hiroshima-based parliamentary career.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed legal studies and entered banking
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from Waseda’s law faculty and joined the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.
